name: United Nations Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework (2026-2030)

framework.name: Strategic Priority 1 High Quality People-Centred Development and Shared Prosperity
framework.description: Aiming to support China’s goal of achieving universal access to high quality social services and social protection, including family and child friendly policies, to improve the quality of life of all people in China, whilst supporting China’s goal of achieving innovation-driven, sustainable and shared economic development and transformation, leading to increased quality employment and livelihood opportunities.

children.name: Outcome 1 By 2030, more people benefit from high-quality, affordable, inclusive and climate-resilient social services and social protection across the life course, with improved well-being, leaving no one behind.

Output 1.1 The Government and other stakeholders demonstrate enhanced capacities to build a resilient health system and deliver high-quality affordable and gender-responsive, health, nutrition and care services accessible to all throughout the life course with an effective multisectoral approach.
Output 1.2 The Government and other stakeholders demonstrate enhanced and resilient capacities to provide high-quality, equitable learning and skills development for all, throughout the life course.
Output 1.3 The Government and other stakeholders demonstrate enhanced capacities to provide universal, high-quality, gender-responsive and climate-smart social protection throughout the life course.

Output 1.4 The Government and other stakeholders demonstrate enhanced capacities to manage the impact of the demographic transition, improving the well-being of all people, for high-quality development.

Output 1.5 The Government and other stakeholders demonstrate enhanced capacities to design and deliver initiatives that promote gender equality and social inclusion, safeguard legal protection, and end discrimination and violence against women and children.

Outcome 2 By 2030, China’s transition to a high-quality and inclusive economic development model characterized by innovation, delivers more balanced sustainable development between rural and urban areas, shared prosperity, decent work, and equitable opportunities for all.

Output 2.1 The Government, private sector and other stakeholders demonstrate enhanced capacities to drive inclusive, resilient and sustainable economic development, including leveraging well-managed human mobility.

Output 2.2 The Government, workers’ and employers’ organisations and other stakeholders demonstrate enhanced capacities to deliver decent work and equitable livelihood opportunities for all, particularly women and those most left behind.

framework.name: Strategic Priority 2 Climate Action and Environmental Sustainability
framework.description: Aiming to support China’s goals and contribution to addressing the three major risks of climate change, biodiversity loss, and environmental pollution.

children.name: Outcome 3 By 2030, all people benefit from China’s accelerated green transition to low-carbon, climate-resilient inclusive, and gender-responsive development and sustainable management of the environment, natural resources and biodiversity.

Output 3.1 Government authorities, the corporate sector and other stakeholders in China demonstrate enhanced capacities to develop and implement inclusive policies to mitigate and adapt to the environmental impact from climate change, including on human mobility.

Output 3.2 China demonstrates enhanced capacities to implement multilateral environmental agreements to effectively address current and emerging environmental, agricultural and health issues with inclusive processes.
Output 3.3 China demonstrates enhanced capacities to use innovative technology applications and related policies to achieve inclusive, low-carbon and nature positive development solutions.

framework.name: Strategic Priority 3 Partnerships to Accelerate Sustainable Development
framework.description: Aiming to leverage China’s commitment to international development cooperation and financing, including through the Global Development Initiative, to advance global progress on the SDGs and multilateral environmental agreements.

children.name: Outcome 4 By 2030, China strengthens its international development cooperation contributions and partnerships towards SDG attainment in line with international norms and standards, with an emphasis on leaving no one and no country behind and gender equality.

Output 4.1 The Government and other institutions in China demonstrate enhanced capacities to develop and deliver demand driven South-South and triangular humanitarian and development cooperation, as well as global public goods in line with international standards.

Output 4.2 China continues to actively contribute to multilateral and bilateral platforms for the advancement of the SDGs and the Pact for the Future, including through the United Nations system and its entities, as well as international cooperation mechanisms such as the Global Development Initiative.

Output 4.3 Government authorities, the corporate and banking sectors in China, including development banks, demonstrate enhanced capacities to develop and implement inclusive SDG-aligned financing and investment strategies and business practices.

Interventions include: (a) facilitate cross-country exchanges and sharing of experiences and  best practices to address development priorities in China, including in relation to population  dynamics and gender-biased sex selection; (b) provide technical support to enhance the  development and delivery of South-South and triangular cooperation initiatives to advance  universal access to sexual and reproductive health and rights and strengthen access to essential  supply needs in partner countries; and (c) engage with the private sector to promote business  practices aligned with the SDGs.

projects.name: UNFPA 1.4.1 Enhanced capacity to manage the impact of the demographic transition
projects.description:
The Government and other partners demonstrate enhanced capacities to manage the impact of the demographic transition, improving the well-being of all people, for high-quality development.
Interventions include: (a) provide technical support for the development and review of  policies and guidelines on ageing, and assessment of its economic and social impacts and  opportunities for the “silver economy,”11 including through the National Transfer Accounts  methodology; (b) conduct analysis of emerging evidence from low-fertility policies that are being  implemented across provinces and promote cross-provincial and cross-country learning and  sharing of good practices; (c) provide advisory support for the generation of population data and  surveys and the collection and analysis of sex- and age-disaggregated data; (d) study the  interactive relationship between population change and economic and social development; (e) conduct analysis of the impact of mega-trends, such as climate change, on sexual and  reproductive health and population dynamics; (f) facilitate platforms to promote intergenerational  solidarity and inform social policies affecting elderly persons and young people; and (g) engage  with the private sector to foster innovative solutions and technologies to bridge the digital divide  and enhance elderly care.
projects.outcome: Output 1.4 The Government and other stakeholders demonstrate enhanced capacities to manage the impact of the demographic transition, improving the well-being of all people, for high-quality development.

projects.name: UNFPA 1.1.1 Enhanced capacity to design and implement policies, programmes and services that promote SRH and gender equality
projects.description:
The Government and other partners demonstrate enhanced capacity to design and implement gender-responsive, evidence-based policies, programmes and services that promote sexual and reproductive health and gender equality, strengthen social inclusion for all, and respond to gender-based violence.
Interventions include:  (a) provide technical advice and document good practices to inform  policies and guidelines for high-quality voluntary family planning services, including on  expanding contraceptive choice and method mix; (b) provide advisory support for scaling up  comprehensive sexuality education to improve the awareness, knowledge and life-skills of young  people to make healthy choices; (c) provide technical advice on the implementation of family 
friendly policies and national laws and policies on preventing and responding to domestic  violence and in addressing gender-biased sex selection in priority provinces; (d) engage with  youth networks and organizations of persons with disabilities to build their leadership skills and  capacity to inform policies and programmes; (e) provide technical support to strengthen the  integration of sexual and reproductive health and protection of women and girls in disaster  preparedness and response; and (f) engage with the private sector to develop innovative solutions  to generate evidence and increase access to information and knowledge on sexual and  reproductive health and rights for young people and vulnerable groups.
projects.outcome: Output 1.1 The Government and other stakeholders demonstrate enhanced capacities to build a resilient health system and deliver high-quality affordable and gender-responsive, health, nutrition and care services accessible to all throughout the life course with an effective multisectoral approach.

projects.name: Enhanced capacity  to design and implement gender-responsive and evidence-based programmes and services that iImprove young people’s development and older persons’ wellbeing in Hainan TAP
projects.description: This output focuses on enhancing the social inclusion and well-being of young people and older persons in Hainan TAP. Aligned with national and local development priorities, this output aims to provide advisory support for increasing access to information and knowledge on sexual and reproductive health and improve the life skills for adolescents and youth through culturally sensitive community-based health promotion and age-appropriate comprehensive sexuality education (CSE) in selected schools. Building on successful experiences from other Tibetan counties in Qinghai Province, local health workers and NGOs will be engaged in delivering these health promotion activities to ensure community reach and relevance. Innovative methods such as livestreaming CSE sessions will be introduced to address barriers related to remoteness and the shortage of trained teachers..Furthermore, the programme will engage with partners to foster innovative solutions and technologies to enhance elderly care.

projects.name: ILO 2.2.6 Policies and strategies adopted and actional programmes implemented for inclusive skills training and lifelong learning and equal employment opportunities for groups at risks of exclusion.
projects.description: China is advancing toward a more inclusive and sustainable labour market by promoting lifelong skills development amid rapid technological and green transitions, yet persistent skills mismatches and limited local-level implementation—especially in digital and green skills—continue to challenge productivity and social inclusion, particularly for persons with disabilities (PWD) and people living with HIV (PLHIV). Building on national initiatives such as Skills for a Brighter Future, the ILO collaborates with government ministries, UN agencies, Disabled Persons’ Federations, and community organizations to strengthen lifelong learning systems, support quality apprenticeships, and expand equitable employment pathways for vulnerable groups. These efforts center on policy advice, practical tools, capacity building, integration of global best practices, and targeted skills training to foster responsive skills policies, inclusive workplaces, and improved employability for all workers.

projects.name: ILO 2.2.1 Tripartite constituents effectively address challenges in the future of work, especially relating to the digital transformation in line with ILS
projects.description: During the 14th Five-Year Plan period, China made steady progress in creating jobs and stabilizing labour markets, strengthening labour protection and reinforcing social dialogue mechanisms. At the same time, China, as one of the world's largest labour markets, is expected to undergo unprecedented structural transformation in the new five year period (2026-2030). Particularly the rapid expansion of new forms of employment and the increasing digitalization of work have begun to reshape conditions of work and employment relationships in China. While digitalization has expanded employment opportunities and flexibility in China, it has also brought new challenges for labour market governance and conditions of work. The growth of platform-based and other digitally mediated work has blurred employment relationships, increased risks related to algorithmic management, working time and income stability, and exposed gaps in labour protection and social security coverage for non-standard forms of workers. These challenges may have differentiated impacts on women workers and workers in vulnerable situations, and require stronger attention to gender equality, social inclusion and non-discrimination. At the same time, the expanding use of artificial intelligence in the world of work raises concerns about job displacement, skills mismatches, transparency, accountability and discrimination, while existing social dialogue mechanisms have yet to fully adapt to the governance of the digital economy and AI. This sub-output aims to further enhance Chinese constituents' capacity to address future of work challenges arising from digital transformation, in line with international labour standards. This includes strengthened capacity for evidence-based policymaking and inclusive social dialogue on employment relationship determination, labour protection for non-standard and platform workers, and the governance of digital technologies and artificial intelligence to promote decent work and social justice, while strengthening legal protection and safeguards against discrimination and violence and harassment.
projects.outcome: Output 2.2 The Government, workers’ and employers’ organisations and other stakeholders demonstrate enhanced capacities to deliver decent work and equitable livelihood opportunities for all, particularly women and those most left behind.

projects.name: ILO 2.2.7 Enhancing Rights Based Disability Inclusive & Sustainable Development in China
projects.description: Stakeholders identify attitudinal barriers as a fundamental obstacle to disability inclusion in China, noting that key government institutions still lack understanding of how these barriers restrict the rights of persons with disabilities, who are often viewed as welfare recipients rather than rights holders. To address this, the programme aims to strengthen knowledge, capacity, and commitment among government bodies, academia, OPDs, and civil society to develop and implement CRPD‑compliant disability‑inclusive policies in areas such as inclusive education, cultural participation, employment, GBV prevention, and access to SRHR. Leveraging the UNPRPD China taskforce as a catalyst, the programme focuses on equipping stakeholders with practical tools for inclusive policymaking, addressing gaps in essential CRPD implementation elements—including equality, accessibility, service delivery, and data—and promoting greater disability inclusion in the CCA and UNSDCF review processes through capacity‑building and dialogue.
